record.paper_title: A review of results and open problems on mathematical models of motion of viscoelastic media of Jeffreys' type
record.original_question: Does the Jeffreys-type system (0.2), (0.4), (0.5), (2.18) admit time-periodic solutions without restrictions on the coefficients, the external force, or the initial data?

evidence.quote: В рамках второй группы важен блок задач о построении хоть каких-нибудь обобщенных решений стационарной краевой задачи и эволюционной4 начально-краевой задачи, а также задача о наличии периодических по времени решений, все — без ограничений на коэффициенты, внешнюю силу и начальные данные.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the following Jeffreys-type model for the motion of an incompressible viscoelastic fluid in a bounded domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ ($n=2,3$) with smooth boundary $\partial\Omega$. The unknowns are the velocity field $v(t,x)\in\mathbb{R}^n$ and the pressure $p(t,x)\in\mathbb{R}$, and the system reads:

(i) Equation of motion:
$$\frac{\partial v}{\partial t} + (v\cdot\nabla) v = \operatorname{Div}\sigma + f,$$

(ii) Incompressibility: $\operatorname{div} v = 0,$

(iii) Constitutive law of Jeffreys type: the deviatoric stress tensor $\tau$ obeys
$$\tau + \lambda_1 \frac{D\tau}{Dt} = 2\eta\Big(\mathcal E(v) + \lambda_2 \frac{D\mathcal E(v)}{Dt}\Big),$$
with total Cauchy stress $\sigma = -pI + \tau$, where $\mathcal E(v)=\tfrac12(\nabla v + (\nabla v)^T)$ is the symmetric strain-rate tensor, $\lambda_1>\lambda_2>0$ are retardation/relaxation times, $\eta>0$ is the viscosity, and $D/Dt$ denotes an objective (e.g. upper- or lower-convected, or Jaumann) time derivative including transport along $v$,

(iv) No-slip boundary condition: $v|_{\partial\Omega}=0,$

(v) The external force $f(t,x)$ is given and time-periodic with period $T>0$, i.e. $f(t+T,x)=f(t,x)$.

Question: Without imposing any smallness or other restrictions on the coefficients $\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\eta$, on the external force $f$, or on the data, does this system always admit at least one (weak) time-periodic solution $(v,p)$ of period $T$?
artifact.status_search_result: Surveys on Jeffreys-type viscoelastic fluid models list the existence of time-periodic solutions without restrictions on coefficients, force, or initial data among the unresolved problems. Web searches return work on related elastic wave equations with viscoelastic terms and on control/throughflow problems for Jeffreys fluids, but no general existence theorem of time-periodic weak solutions for the full Jeffreys system without smallness or regularity restrictions has been located. The status appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Existence and stability of time periodic solutions to nonlinear elastic wave equations with viscoelastic terms
status_evidence.snippet: Time-periodic solutions are studied for nonlinear elastic wave equations with viscoelastic terms; addresses related but distinct setting.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work treats time-periodic solutions for related viscoelastic-type equations, indicating activity but not resolving the Jeffreys fluid case in full generality.

status_evidence.title: On the control of viscoelastic Jeffreys fluids
status_evidence.snippet: Studies controllability questions for Jeffreys-type fluids; existence theory for the full nonlinear system remains delicate.
status_evidence.claim: Mathematical theory for Jeffreys-type viscoelastic systems is still developing; periodic existence in full generality is not established.
